key_insight: DrugHarness turns execution feedback into reviewed, condition-specific skills that guide later computational drug-discovery tasks.
engineering_relevance: The harness combines composable scientific tools, linked experimental artifacts and evidence-checked skill updates to support adaptable discovery workflows.
method: Integrate over 80 scientific operations with biomedical resources and task-specific code.
Induce candidate skills with observable applicability conditions, recommended actions and supporting evidence.
Use an independent agent to verify sources and, when needed, run targeted trials before admitting skills.
evidence_signal: On retrospective skill-development tasks, evolution raised Qwen’s affinity-comparison accuracy from 62.2% to 81.1%; in a prospective HPK1 study, a synthesized compound achieved cellular IC50 of 14.19 nM, a 2.64-fold potency improvement over the best input reference.
watch_item: Retrospective skill-development gains and one prospective HPK1 study do not establish generalization across unseen targets or discovery settings.
paper_title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
